recipes.name: Chicken and Ham Casserole
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup cooked, cubed chicken breast meat

steps.text: Preheat oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Melt butter in a large saucepan over low heat. Stir in the flour and heat until bubbly. Slowly add the milk, stirring constantly, until mixture is thickened and smooth.
Remove from heat and stir in the chicken, ham, noodles, celery, salt and ground black pepper. Transfer this mixture to a 1 1/2 quart casserole dish.

Bake at 400 degrees F (200 degrees C) for 15 minutes. Remove from oven, sprinkle with the cheese and top with paprika, as desired. Return to oven and bake for 5 to 10 minutes, or until cheese is bubbly.

raw_recipe.headline: Chicken and Ham Casserole
raw_recipe.description: An assemblage of leftover chicken and ham, some noodles and vegetables, a little cheese--just about whatever you have on hand will work in this casserole.

review.reviewBody: Took the advice from other reviewers and doubled up on this yummy recipe plus added a can of "healthy" cream of mushroom soup. Didn't use the celery but used green pepper and asparagus. Some garlic and onion powder added to the flavor. Once assembled I shredded cheddar cheese on top and sprinkled with bread crumbs and dotted with butter. The whole family loved it!

I added mushrooms and used arborio rice and gouda cheese. It was great. This recipe can be amended and changed in many ways. Cheese can vary, meats can change, a dash of white wine or broth would work. Red or green peppers could be added for some color. I also used an iron skillet for sautéing and for baking--cuts down on pots needed. I made rice but this would be a good use for rice left over from Chinese carry-out.

I thought this was much better than I was expecting. I cooked an onion and garlic in a pan with no oil and did add it into the mixture. I also added dry mustard, oregano and cayenne pepper. I had to use spaghetti noodles because that's all I had. And I did add the can of mushroom soup like many suggested. The only ham I had was sliced deli ham but I used some of it and I liked it.

My husband isn't a big fan of chicken. I doubled the recipe. I added velvetta cheese to the butter, flour and milk and poured over ham, chicken and sauteed onions. Deleted the noodles and served over rice. Tasted like chicken cordon blue.

This turned out very good. I used about 2 cups of cooked noodles, 1 cup chicken, and 1 cup ham. I also added 1 cup of frozen mixed vegetables. With those changes, it's a good meal for two people. I lowered the calorie count by using skim milk and fat free cheese. Still tasted great! The paprika adds a nice flavor.

This was a really good comfort food! Even hubby liked it and he is not a casserole person. I did take some other reviewers suggestions. I added garlic powder, dry mustard and crushed red paper flakes (didn't have cayenne pepper) to the the milk mixture. Then I added a can of cream of mushroom soup. I didn't have any celery so I used some leftover green beans and wax beans for color. I also used panko flakes/bread crumbs with the cheese mixture. A keeper in our house!!!
Very yummy! Replaced the milk with a can of mushroom soup. Added a chopped onion, chives, and terragon. Did not have celery, but turned out great! This is a keeper!

It wasn't bad. It needs more "spice" in my opinion. I added a can of Cream of Mushroom soup, from the advice of a previous reviewer, and also added some mixed vegetables. I may make this again but add more things here and there to add more taste to it.

Definitely a keeper! Had to make twice in 3 days! Using hints from previous reviews: added 1/2 teaspoon dry mustard, 1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper, sliced fresh mushrooms; doubled the noodles; added 1/2 can cream of mushroom soup. BIG hit!!!!

I get amused at the reviews. Some change them so much that there is littleof the original left. I substituted the equivalent of !/2 package of leftover cheese mac with burger for the noodles, added cream of chicken soup for the sauce, left out the chicken, added sauteed onion and broccoli and celery, topped with cream of chicken soup and Panko bread crumbs, shredded cheddar,ample pepper and paprika, baked in medium dish for 30 minutes then a little longer, then served. Everyone liked it. Wonderful recipe. Thanks so much.
I mostly stuck to the recipe, subbed broccoli for celery. My 3 year old notorious fussy eater gobbled it up and asked for seconds 😱
Very good simple casserole. Please note that this recipe is for two servings. And it’s a perfect size for two.

Oh my goodness...this was the best and easiest casserole I've had in ages. Made the recipe exactly as stated and have saved it in my own personal recipe book as I plan to make this many, many more times. Maybe next time I just may add a few more veggies to the mix just to experiment but this recipe totally stands on it's own for sure. Love!

This was good but not great. I felt that the recipe had 3 flaws - too much ham, too much sauce and not enough noodles. Thankfully I had cooked extra noodles so I added them in but it still wasn't enough. And the ham overpowered the dish...it's all I could taste. I might make again but will modify accordingly. Couldn't eat it again as written.

This is a good casserole to use up leftovers. In my case, I used all ham in the recipe. I increased the ingredients to make servings for 6 as I wanted to freeze a small casserole dish. This dish came together easily and was enjoyed by my family. I would make this again if I had ham and or chicken to use up. I served this with lettuce salad and green beans.

Thought I would try this, as I needed to use up some leftover ham and chicken. It turned out ok although very creamy which didn't appeal and also it lacked something, but not sure what. My husband loved it however but I told him to enjoy, as he won't be seeing it on the table again. ;-)

yummy!!!!!!!!
i sustituted the celery for raw greenbeans and instead of parika i sprinkled ground cayanne pepper on top. also, you can use any mild cheese

I read several times that this recipe would not feed 4 people--well it says it serves 2. Which I was looking for. I used spinach noodles, sauted onion, yellow pepper & mushrooms. Made the white sauce as read. Added toasted slivered almonds. Did use Panko--as I always do for bread crumbs on top of anything. Didn't taste like leftovers at all! Even some left over for hubby's lunch tomorrow. Worked for me!

I thought this was really yummy. I just used ham (trying to get rid of some leftovers). I added a little cheese to the "sauce" after it had thickened up (a little velveeta because that's what I had). Also added some seasoning to the white sauce (paprika, red pepper, black pepper). This was a hearty, comforting sort of casserole. Very good!

After reading all of the good reviews, I chose not to believe the not-so-good ones. But this recipe most definitely was too bland for my taste, even after I added more spices than listed. The broccoli I added gave it most of it's flavour really, so that's not saying much. I'll be looking for a different recipe next time..
